headline: Oct 31: Medical tests for Malaysia-bound workers to begin
summary: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment announced that approved medical centers will conduct the exams.
details: Medical examinations for Bangladeshi workers intending to go to Malaysia will start on October 31.
The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment announced this in a press release on Wednesday.
Tests will be conducted only at approved medical centers, the list of which will soon be published on the ministry's website.
The ministry warned that any medical tests conducted before this date will not be accepted.
Furthermore, such tests will not be processed for immigration clearance.
Workers are urged to regularly check the ministry's website for the list of approved medical centers to ensure their documentation is valid.
caption:

headline_marked: Mushfiqur Rahim [[ruled out of first Test]] against West Indies
headline: Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of first Test against West Indies
summary: The veteran batter sustains a hand injury during training, forcing Towhid Hridoy to step in for the series opener in Mirpur.
details: Veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim was ruled out of the first Test against the West Indies at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur after sustaining a hand injury during training.
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first, with Towhid Hridoy replacing the injured Mushfiqur in the playing XI.
Shoriful Islam also made a return to the side, replacing Ebadot Hossain, while the team retained all three spinners from the recent Afghanistan match.
The Tigers are looking to bounce back from a disappointing tour of the UAE, where they suffered defeats in the ODI tri-series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan.
Motivation for the team is high as they are currently fourth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings and are aiming to qualify for the final at The Oval in June.
To keep their hopes of reaching the final alive, Bangladesh will need to win at least four of their remaining six Tests, including the series opener in Mirpur.
caption:
A major blow for the Tigers! Mushfiqur Rahim is out of the first Test due to a hand injury.

Veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim was ruled out of the first Test against the West Indies at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur after sustaining a hand injury during training.

Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first, with Towhid Hridoy replacing the injured Mushfiqur in the playing XI.

Shoriful Islam also made a return to the side, replacing Ebadot Hossain, while the team retained all three spinners from the recent Afghanistan match.

The Tigers are looking to bounce back from a disappointing tour of the UAE, where they suffered defeats in the ODI tri-series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan.

Motivation for the team is high as they are currently fourth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings and are aiming to qualify for the final at The Oval in June.

To keep their hopes of reaching the final alive, Bangladesh will need to win at least four of their remaining six Tests, including the series opener in Mirpur.
